references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says exactly the same thing: 'All things have been handed over to me by my Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.'
Jesus declares that all authority in heaven and on earth has been given to him, which corresponds to 'all things have been handed over to me by my Father' in Luke 10:22.
John testifies that the Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand, consistent with the idea that all things have been handed over to Jesus by the Father.
Jesus knew that the Father had given all things into his hands, reflecting the same handing over of all things from the Father to the Son.
The Father has given the Son authority over all people, emphasizing that all things have been handed over to him by the Father.

No one has ever seen God, but the only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has made him known – this corresponds to no one knowing the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.
Jesus says, 'As the Father knows me, so I know the Father,' expressing the mutual, exclusive knowledge between Father and Son described in Luke 10:22.
No one has seen the Father except the one who is from God – he has seen the Father. This underscores the Son's unique knowledge of the Father.
Jesus says to Philip, 'Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.' The Son reveals the Father to those he chooses, as described in Luke 10:22.
Paul writes that God has put all things under Christ's feet, which connects to the idea that all things have been handed over to the Son by the Father.

Jesus says that the world has not known the Father, but he knows him and has made the Father's name known to his disciples – this corresponds to the Son's role as the only one who knows and reveals the Father.
The Son of Man is given dominion, glory, and a kingdom by the Ancient of Days, pointing forward to all things being handed over to the Son by the Father.
Jesus tells Peter that it was not flesh and blood that revealed this to him, but the Father's revelation through the Son, connecting to the idea that the Son reveals to whomever he chooses.
God raised Christ from the dead and set him above all powers and put all things under his feet, emphasizing that all things have been handed over to the Son by the Father.
